organization: Health and Welfare Council of Long Island
program: Benefits enrollment and HEALI social-care network coordination

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-sixth-seventh-independent-acceptance.json: primary-source checks, independent reconstruction of every scenario, and explicit uncertainty review; accepted as conditional alpha modeling, not measured causal impact.

what: HWCLI helps Long Island residents enroll in benefits and coordinates the HEALI social-care network.
The health model covers additional insurance access and a narrowly discounted nutrition-services pathway in Nassau and Suffolk counties.
The central model implies about $50.2 million per10 NYC-MSA QALYs.
strengths: Clear Nassau/Suffolk service footprint inside the MSA.
An operating public-benefits and social-care infrastructure can connect otherwise missed residents to services.
The model separates recipient coordination credit, alternative help and marginal funding.
reservations: The 2025 report reproduces a financial activity statement labeled 2024, so forward cost is uncertain.
Network service counts are not unique improved-health beneficiaries.
No measured unrestricted-gift elasticity or recipient-specific utility effect establishes the central judgments.

sections.what:
HWCLI provides benefits navigation and leads HEALI. HEALI contracts with providers and coordinates services; eligible care is Medicaid-covered. Nassau and Suffolk are both in the defined MSA. [Network structure](https://healiny.org/about/)

The report records 4,891 insurance enrollments and 7,000 network nutrition services in 2025. These are distinct model inputs, not health outcomes. [2025 report](https://hwcli.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/FINAL-2025-HWCLI-ANNUAL-REPORT.pdf)
sections.monitoring: Track completed coverage, genuinely otherwise-uninsured months, distinct nutrition recipients and completed service intensity, plus pre/post utility with comparison groups. Do not count screenings, benefit dollars or referrals as QALYs. Oregon randomized evidence found improved mental health but no significant measured physical-health improvements at two years; our 0.01 annual utility assumption is an explicit transfer judgment, not a trial coefficient. [Original trial](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMsa1212321)
sections.qualitative: Coordination may reduce language and administrative barriers, but providers, public insurers and other navigators remain active without a new gift. The network's own description confirms multiple independent partners and Medicaid financing; HWCLI cannot receive all network health credit. Unmodeled housing, maternal-health and advocacy outcomes are set net zero, not established absent. [HEALI](https://healiny.org/about/)
sections.cost: Central cost is $10,313,844: twice $5,156,922 historical whole-recipient expense for forward SCN ramp-up. Health=.25×[4,891×.3×.01×.5 +7,000×.25×.5×.02×.5×.2×.5]=2.0528750000000002 MSA QALYs, or $50,240,974 per 10. The final 0.5 nutrition factor removes potential overlap with coverage utility. All causal conversion factors are judgments. For an illustrative $1,000 gift, whole-portfolio scaling corresponds to 0.474 historical enrollments and 0.679 network nutrition units before additionality/attribution adjustments; these are normalized activity equivalents, not promises or measured unit costs. No mortality benefit, perpetual benefit or public treatment savings is added. Partner and public medical costs are outside recipient cost.
sections.funding:
The original annual report lists $5,156,922 expenses, including $2,472,321 personnel/fringe and $2,684,601 nonpersonnel, in its activity statement labeled 2024 despite a 2025-financials heading. We preserve the statement year and do not treat this as an audited 2025 cost. Its balance-sheet/net-asset figures conflict internally and are not used for a reserve estimate. No three-year mean is established. [Financial page](https://hwcli.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/FINAL-2025-HWCLI-ANNUAL-REPORT.pdf)

An unrestricted gift is modeled as following the whole portfolio, with only 25% incremental capacity after substitute grants, public funding and reserves. Neither that fraction nor the forward multiplier is observed. The website has a donation link, but there is no verified restricted marginal offer. [Official site](https://hwcli.com/)

model.costScope: Whole-recipient 2024 reported activity expense times explicit forward-cost multiplier 2; not network-wide social cost. No expense denominator from older cost is silently paired with new ramp-up output.
model.geographicAttribution: g=1 for modeled Nassau/Suffolk pathways, both MSA member counties; no headquarters inference.
model.formula: Q=g*b*(E*a*u*t+N*d*c*v*s*k*z); cost=C*f; price10=10*cost/Q. z removes nutrition utility already captured in coverage term; mortality=0.
model.counterfactual: Existing Medicaid care, the SCN, partners and alternative enrollment help continue. Coverage additionality .3, nutrition alternative-care .5, HWCLI attribution .2 and funding .25 are separate judgments; no blanket public baseline credit.
model.attribution: Insurance term .3 credits genuinely additional coverage; network term .2 reserves 80% of incremental network health for delivery partners and other actors. Both multiplied by .25 capacity additionality of ordinary gifts. Nutrition utility multiplied by nonoverlap z=.5, separate from HWCLI causal share and financing additionality.
model.uncertainty: Very weak-confidence subjective scenarios; no recipient QALY trial. Cost-year mismatch, repeat service intensity and marginal public-finance substitution dominate.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional insured person-years and distinct sustained nutrition recipients; health utility limited to half a year; mortality credit zero.

inputs.name: f
inputs.rationale: 2x historical expense allows public-SCN ramp-up; not a measured budget.

inputs.name: E
inputs.rationale: 4,891 completed enrollments, not necessarily newly insured.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: 30%coverage beyond other navigators, self-enrollment and existing cover.

inputs.name: u
inputs.rationale: .01 finite quality-of-life gain; weak transfer assumption, not trial coefficient.

inputs.name: t
inputs.rationale: .5year average useful coverage; no lifetime continuation.

inputs.name: N
inputs.rationale: 7,000 reported units, not automatically unique recipients.

inputs.name: d
inputs.unit: distinct sustained recipients per nutrition unit
inputs.rationale: .25 converts4units to one sustained recipient; unverified intensity.

inputs.name: c
inputs.rationale: .5 discounts food support obtainable without network.

inputs.name: v
inputs.rationale: .02 small health utility assumed among effectively served recipients.

inputs.name: s
inputs.rationale: .5year finite duration; not a permanent disease cure.

inputs.name: k
inputs.unit: HWCLI share of incremental network health
inputs.rationale: .2 reserves80%for partners and other contributing actors.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: .25 allows replacement public grants, reserves and other funding.

inputs.name: g
inputs.rationale: Modeled services in Nassau/Suffolk; both counties insideMSA.

inputs.name: z
inputs.unit: nutrition utility not overlapping coverage utility
inputs.rationale: Half of nutrition utility removed to avoid overlap with health captured by enrollment; no beneficiary linkage obtained.

sensitivity: Doubling the central forward multiplier from 2 to 4 doubles price; this explicitly tests 2025 ramp-up cost mismatch.
Setting b, additional coverage, or utility to zero removes their pathway benefit. Network attribution cannot be assumed 100%.
Other harms exceeding 2.0528750000000002 incremental QALYs erase central health; zero omitted-portfolio health is not a lower bound.
Nutrition nonoverlap z ranges0–1; central.5. Enrollment and nutrition records are not linked, so disjoint benefit is not presumed.
